props.title: Dead Snow
props.initialSlug: Nazi zombies terrorize students in snowy Norway

sections.content: **Dead Snow** (2009) brilliantly combines Nazi zombies with Norwegian snow-covered landscapes, marking a standout entry in horror-comedy. Director Tommy Wirkola channels both Sam Raimi's **Evil Dead II** (1987) and Peter Jackson's **Braindead** (1992) with gleefully excessive gore and pitch-black humor. The film follows medical students on a ski vacation who encounter frozen Wehrmacht soldiers rising from their icy graves. It revolutionized zombie horror by introducing World War II historical elements into the undead formula, paving the way for films like **Overlord** (2018).

sections.content: The success of **Dead Snow** sparked a renaissance in Nazi zombie films, though none matched its perfect blend of horror and humor. **Frankenstein's Army** (2013) took the concept into found footage territory, while **Outpost** (2008) played it straight as a supernatural military thriller. The subgenre traces back to **Shock Waves** (1977), featuring Peter Cushing as a Nazi scientist whose underwater zombie experiments resurface. SUBHEAD: Snow-Based Horror Evolution

Winter horror settings gained new life after **Dead Snow**. **The Thing** (1982) established the isolation-in-snow template, but recent entries like **30 Days of Night** (2007) and **Let the Right One In** (2008) prove snow's effectiveness for horror. The stark white landscape creates perfect contrast for blood and violence while amplifying the sense of isolation that **Dead Snow** uses masterfully.
